title: High-Compatibility Variable-Stiffness Trunk Rehabilitation Robot
summary: Variable-stiffness design and dynamic compliant control for personalized trunk rehabilitation.
image_alt: Abstract graphic for the trunk rehabilitation robot project
funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China, Young Scientists Fund (C), No. 52505044
overview: This project investigates high-compatibility variable-stiffness design and dynamic compliant control for trunk rehabilitation robots. It builds on prior work in wearable robotic braces, serial–parallel mechanisms, and robot-assisted trunk assessment.
challenge: A trunk rehabilitation robot must provide adequate support across changing postures and impairment levels while remaining comfortable, safe, and mechanically compatible with human motion.
approach: The project combines variable-stiffness mechanism design, dynamic compliant control, biomechanical modeling, and experimental evaluation with rehabilitation users.

title: Robot Technologies for Active Rehabilitation of Lumbar Disc Herniation
summary: Robot design, control, and evaluation methods for active rehabilitation of lumbar disc herniation.
image_alt: Abstract graphic for the lumbar rehabilitation robot project
overview: This project develops key robotic technologies for active rehabilitation of lumbar disc herniation, connecting compliant physical assistance with measurable rehabilitation training.
challenge: Lumbar rehabilitation requires assistance that supports training goals without imposing rigid motion or excessive physical load on the user.
approach: Research activities span wearable mechanism design, assistance control, biomechanical measurement, and prototype evaluation.

title: Rigid–Flexible Coupled Variable-Stiffness Lumbar Rehabilitation Robot
summary: A high-compatibility lumbar rehabilitation robot using rigid–flexible coupled actuation and variable stiffness.
image_alt: Abstract graphic for the variable-stiffness lumbar robot project
overview: The project explores rigid–flexible coupled actuation for a high-compatibility, variable-stiffness lumbar rehabilitation robot.
challenge: Wearable lumbar systems need to balance support capacity, stiffness range, compact structure, and compatibility with complex torso motion.
approach: The work integrates variable-stiffness actuation, compact mechanism optimization, compliant control, and experimental characterization.
